title: Senior Deep Learning Software Engineer, Inference and Model Optimization
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA is at the forefront of the generative AI revolution! The Algorithmic Model Optimization Team specifically focuses on optimizing generative AI models such as large language models (LLM) and diffusion models for maximal inference efficiency using techniques ranging from neural architecture search and pruning to sparsity, quantization, and automated deployment strategies. Our work includes conducting applied research to improve model efficiency as well as developing an innovative software platform (TRT Model Optimizer). Our software is used both internally across NVIDIA and externally by research and engineering teams alike developing best-in-class AI models.


We are now looking for a Senior Deep Learning Software Engineer to develop and scale up our automated inference and deployment solution. As part of the team, you will be instrumental in pushing the limits of inference efficiency and large-scale, automated deployment. Your work will touch upon fundamental aspects of a typical machine learning stack including working in high-level frameworks like PyTorch and HuggingFace to developing and improving high-performance kernel implementations in CUDA, TRT-LLM, and Triton. This is an exceptional opportunity for passionate software engineers straddling the boundaries of research and engineering, with a strong background in both machine learning fundamentals and software architecture & engineering.


What you’ll be doing:

  • Train, develop, and deploy state-of-the generative AI models like LLMs and diffusion models using NVIDIA's AI software stack.
  • Leverage and build upon the torch 2.0 ecosystem (TorchDynamo, torch.export, torch.compile, etc...) to analyze and extract standardized model graph representation from arbitrary torch models for our automated deployment solution.
  • Develop high-performance optimization techniques for inference, such as automated model sharding techniques (e.g. tensor parallelism, sequence parallelism), efficient attention kernels with kv-caching, and more.
  • Collaborate with teams across NVIDIA to use performant kernel implementations within our automated deployment solution.
  • Analyze and profile GPU kernel-level performance to identify hardware and software optimization opportunities.
  • Continuously innovate on the inference performance to ensure NVIDIA's inference software solutions (TRT, TRT-LLM, TRT Model Optimizer) can maintain and increase its leadership in the market.
  • Play a pivotal role in architecting and designing a modular and scalable software platform to provide an excellent user experience with broad model support and optimization techniques to increase adoption.

What we need to see:

  • Masters, PhD, or equivalent experience in Computer Science, AI, Applied Math, or related field.
  • 8+ years of relevant work or research experience in Deep Learning.
  • Excellent software design skills, including debugging, performance analysis, and test design.
  • Strong proficiency in Python, PyTorch, and related ML tools (e.g. HuggingFace).
  • Strong algorithms and programming fundamentals.
  • Good written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Contributions to PyTorch, JAX, or other Machine Learning Frameworks.
  • Knowledge of GPU architecture and compilation stack, and capability of understanding and debugging end-to-end performance.
  • Familiarity with NVIDIA's deep learning SDKs such as TensorRT.
  • Prior experience in writing high-performance GPU kernels for machine learning workloads in frameworks such as CUDA, CUTLASS, or Triton.

We are looking for software engineering interns for our Sparse Linear Algebra team, which develops libraries like cuSPARSE that are a key part of high-performance computing and deep learning software stacks. The main purpose of these libraries is to provide the fastest computing primitives for operations like sparse matrix-vector and sparse matrix-matrix products, among many others. We see strong interest in optimization of such key functionalities from various industrial and research organizations - from gaming and machine learning to autonomous driving and chip modeling. All of these operations need to be optimized for current and future GPUs and for a wide range of unstructured sparse matrix inputs, which can also necessitate changing the underlying algorithms mathematically and using techniques like code/kernel generation. Does the idea of being at the heart of these projects and applying your knowledge to develop and optimize algorithms which make an impact around world excite you? If yes, then come and join our team!


During your internship, you will work with senior software engineers on the libraries team who will provide mentorship and guide you in developing highly optimized algorithms. Projects will involve implementing new numerical algorithms, defining APIs, analyzing performance, finding appropriate solutions for difficult numerical corner cases, and other general software engineering work.


What you'll be doing:

  • Analyze the performance of GPU implementations and find opportunities for improvements
  • Collaborate with team members to understand software use cases and requirements

What we need to see:

  • Pursuing MS or PhD in Computational Science, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, or equivalent program area.
  • Strong C++ programming, debugging, performance analysis, and test design skills
  • Experience implementing sparse linear algebra algorithms
  • Parallel programming experience using CUDA and/or OpenMP
  • Experience with domain-specific language design, code/kernel generation, and compiler optimizations

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

title: Research Scientist, Autonomous Systems and Physical AI Research - PhD New College Grad 2026
descriptionHtml:
We are now recruiting top Research Scientists to work on autonomous vehicles, robotics, and physical AI! Intelligent machines that can perceive, reason, and safely interact with people and the physical world are rapidly becoming a reality. Self-driving cars, autonomous delivery and construction vehicles, mobile manipulators, and other robotic systems are moving closer to widespread deployment. However, fundamental research challenges remain before these systems can operate safely, reliably, and autonomously in complex, unfamiliar environments.


For example, how can we:

  • Develop new training paradigms that use perception and interaction to train autonomous vehicle and robot policies in closed loop?
  • Equip autonomous systems with online and offline assurances that meet the requirements of safety-critical applications?
  • Enable vehicles and robots to navigate across new environments, tasks, and embodiments?
  • Build systems that reason under uncertainty and interact safely and naturally with people and other agents?

These are some of the exciting questions being explored by NVIDIA’s Autonomous Systems and Physical AI Research (ASPIRE) group. Our diverse, interdisciplinary team conducts foundational research spanning foundation model design, embodied reasoning, safety, closed-loop training and evaluation, and agentic workflows for Physical AI development. We also investigate related areas including decision-making under uncertainty, deep learning, reinforcement learning, simulation, and the verification and validation of safety-critical AI systems. Our focus is on fundamental research, and lab members are encouraged to publish their work and open-source their code. NVIDIA is known for its collaborative culture, and our researchers work closely with experts across the company in autonomous vehicles, robotics, perception, simulation, and machine learning. This creates opportunities to influence real-world products while retaining the freedom and bandwidth to conduct groundbreaking, publishable research.


What you'll be doing:

  • Designing and implementing cutting-edge techniques for autonomous vehicles, robotics, and physical AI.
  • Conducting original research and publishing your results.
  • Collaborating with research colleagues, internal product teams, and external researchers.
  • Transferring technology you’ve developed to relevant product groups.

What we need to see:

  • Completing or recently completed a PhD in 2026 in Robotics, Computer Science, Computer Engineering or a related field.
  • Relevant research experience in autonomous vehicles, robotics, embodied AI, or autonomous systems.
  • Strong knowledge of the theory and practice of vehicle or robot autonomy—or expertise in a related area, with a strong interest in applying your work to autonomous systems.
  • A track record of research excellence, demonstrated through publications at leading conferences and journals—such as RSS, ICRA, CoRL, IJRR, NeurIPS, ICML, CVPR, TAC, etc.—and through other research artifacts such as open-source software.
  • Exceptional Python programming skills; experience with C++ and parallel programming, such as CUDA, is a plus.
  • Experience with machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills are required, along with the ability to thrive in a dynamic, research-focused team.

title: Senior High Speed IO Validation Engineer
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. Today, we are tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing — an era in which our GPUs act as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that understand the world. Doing what has never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent.


NVIDIA’s Silicon Co-Design Group is the team that gets every GPU, SoC, and CPU silicon program from first power-on to high-volume production. We are hiring an HSIO Validation Engineer to own characterization and qualification of high-speed I/Os — PCIe, NVLink, NVLink-C2C, UCIe, USB, UFS, and Ethernet — on brand-new silicon serving datacenter, AI, and client markets. Your bench is where silicon meets the signal — where every link train, jitter sweep, eye diagram, and protocol corner gets exercised before the part ships. You drive characterization and debug for IO interconnects across silicon, board, firmware, and driver — designing tests that anticipate rack-scale deployment so marginality surfaces at die-and-board scale, never in a rack. Your decisions show up in link margin, BER, power per lane, and the go/no-go calls that gate samples and production.


What you will be doing:

  • Own end-to-end characterization and validation of high-speed IO — PCIe, NVLink, NVLink-C2C, UCIe, USB, UFS, Ethernet — from silicon die through package and board, on NVIDIA GPUs, CPUs, and SoCs.
  • Develop and execute validation test plans for silicon and SoC-level HSIO features — bring-up, corner qualification, stress, productization, and structured DOE across PVT, board, cable/connector, thermal, and firmware variables — left-shifting silicon failures before deployment.
  • Drive power characterization and optimization across IO interconnects under workload-representative stimuli (MLPerf-class patterns at silicon/board level) — analyze trade-offs across V/F, lane config, and protocol state — and feed back into design, firmware, and binning.
  • Drive systematic root-cause analysis for complex HSIO bugs — isolating contributions across silicon, package, board, firmware, and driver, with platform/thermal/mechanical partners when system context matters. Convert rack-observed failures into silicon/board reproducers so future spins fix the root cause upstream.
  • Assess manufacturing and yield implications of HSIO margin distributions — identify gaps in scaling from chip to product, and feed back into binning and design.
  • Develop and improve validation methodologies, automation frameworks, and margin-tracking infrastructure — increase efficiency and coverage as platform complexity grows.

What we need to see:

  • BS or MS in Electrical or Computer Engineering (or equivalent), with 6+ years in post-silicon HSIO validation, characterization, or a closely related discipline.
  • Deep understanding of high-speed serial link protocols (PCIe Gen5+, NVLink, NVLink-C2C, UCIe, CXL) and the underlying SERDES architecture — equalization, link training, electrical characterization — with strong signal integrity and jitter knowledge.
  • Strong SI and PI fundamentals — S-parameters, eye diagrams, channel margin, crosstalk, return loss, PDN noise, jitter decomposition — and validation experience across silicon and platform boundaries (CoWoS/interposer/substrate, board), translating rack-environment effects into silicon/board characterization.
  • Hands-on with lab instrumentation (DSOs, BERTs, VNAs, protocol/logic analyzers, TDR), DOE/shmoo/margin-trending, and Python-based test automation — with a track record of driving cross-functional debug across chip, package, board, firmware, driver, and system teams.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Hands-on experience with PCIe Gen5/Gen6 or NVLink validation on production silicon — link training, equalization tuning, BER margining, or compliance debug.
  • Prior SERDES, mixed-signal, or analog circuit design experience — sufficient to independently form hypotheses, design Sim-to-Si correlation experiments, and propose silicon/system-side fixes during debug.
  • Track record of translating rack-environment conditions (thermal, connector reliability, neighbor noise) into silicon/board characterization — finding marginality at die-and-board scale before it appears in the field.
  • Comfortable using AI productivity tools (Claude, Copilot, or equivalent) to compress log triage, regression analysis, scripting, and reporting workflows.

title: Senior Technical Product Manager, Infrastructure Resilience
descriptionHtml:
We're building software that helps cloud partners and operators understand why AI workloads fail and keep GPU clusters ready for work. You'll bring deep experience in GPU cluster operations to help automate investigations across hardware and software. Working with engineering and operations teams, you'll turn those findings into product priorities. We're hiring a Technical Product Manager to own AI infrastructure resilience platform capabilities and developer experience, including GPU node health contracts and interfaces, workload failure attribution, and the open-source software that operators and cloud partners build on. You will own the roadmap and work directly with the engineering and operations communities that deploy and extend this software. This role contributes to NVIDIA's open, modular infrastructure software for designing, operating, and optimizing AI factories at scale.

We encourage technical product managers, architects, site reliability engineers, and infrastructure engineers who understand the management of GPU clusters and want to help operators solve these problems to apply.

What you'll be doing:

  • Own the product vision, roadmap, and delivery priorities for AI infrastructure resilience, partnering with engineering on architecture and execution.
  • Work with customers and partners to identify gaps in GPU cluster operations and define platform capabilities that address them. Help operators assess node readiness and distinguish hardware failures from application failures, while shaping which signals are available through public interfaces or extensions that require additional access.
  • Work directly with cloud partners and cluster operators to translate their operational requirements into platform capabilities.
  • Lead community engagement for open-source platform projects, including contribution models, ecosystem partnerships, and developer adoption.

What we need to see:

  • 12+ years of experience across product management, solutions architecture, software engineering, or site reliability engineering on technical infrastructure products. Technical depth in GPU or AI infrastructure is required.
  • Knowledge of GPU failure modes: XID codes, ECC correctable and uncorrectable errors, DCGM metrics, NVLink and PCIe health signals.
  • Understanding of why AI workloads fail and GPU nodes become unavailable for scheduling. This includes distributed training failures (NCCL timeouts and framework errors), distinguishing hardware from application faults, scheduler health and drain behavior, and interpreting signals from DCGM, sysfs, and dmesg.
  • Demonstrated ability to work with senior technical customers and translate operational requirements into product decisions.
  • Strong written and verbal communication across technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or equivalent experience.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Hands-on experience as a site reliability or infrastructure engineer supporting GPU clusters. You have triaged workload failures, interpreted XID logs, and worked across teams to investigate failed training runs spanning thousands of GPUs.
  • Deep familiarity with GPU scheduling, topology-aware placement, or multi-tenant GPU cluster management: Slurm prolog/epilog, Kueue, or Kubernetes-native scheduler environments.
  • Experience building products that produce structured diagnostics or attribution output: health verdict schemas, log analysis pipelines, rules-engine systems, or observability APIs at data center scale.
  • Practical experience delivering or contributing to an open-source infrastructure project, including managing contributor engagement on GitHub.

Known throughout the tech industry as a highly sought-after employer, NVIDIA delivers highly competitive salaries and an extensive benefits package. As you consider your future, explore what we can provide for you and your family at www.nvidiabenefits.com/

title: Mixed-Signal Design Engineer – RTL and Co-Simulation
descriptionHtml:

The digital RTL implements the full control loop, including protections, fault handling, and calibration. This is a unique role with complete system-level exposure and the opportunity to influence both analog and digital design. The engineer should be flexible as priorities shift between co-simulation, RTL development, and debugging.

NVIDIA is a “learning machine” that constantly evolves by adapting to new opportunities that are hard to solve, that only we can address, and that matter to the world. What you'll be doing:

  • Build and run co-simulations that connect digital RTL with analog circuits or SPICE and Verilog-A models.
  • Enhance and maintain the RTL for the power controller’s full digital control loop.
  • Verify startup, steady-state, transient, calibration, and fault behavior at the system level in either a purely digital or a co-simulation environment.
  • Debug issues across the analog–digital boundary with analog and digital designers.
  • Develop RTL behavioral models for mixed-signal blocks.
  • Design and implement control, protection, fault-handling, and calibration features.

What we need to see:

  • B.S. or MS degree in Electrical Engineering (or equivalent experience)
  • 1-3 years of work on analog–digital co-simulation and digital RTL design for a power controller.
  • Experience designing and debugging synthesizable Verilog or SystemVerilog RTL.
  • Flexibility to work across co-simulation and RTL design as project priorities change.
  • A strong inclination to learn how the analog circuitry behaves. Analog expertise is not required; the team will provide support to help you ramp up.
  • Strong teamwork and outstanding interpersonal skills.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

title: Deep Learning Model and System Optimization Engineering Intern – 2027
descriptionHtml:
We are now looking for a Deep Learning Performance Engineer Intern to join our team. Large language models are transforming how people interact with computing, while placing unprecedented demands on inference performance, memory efficiency, scalability, and deployment cost.


Our team develops GPU-accelerated software for deep learning inference. We work across model architectures, algorithms, numerical representations, inference systems, and GPU architectures to continuously improve the performance and deployment capabilities of large language models on NVIDIA GPUs. Our work contributes to inference frameworks such as TensorRT-LLM and helps bring state-of-the-art models to production efficiently. We are looking for outstanding interns who are passionate about large language model inference, low-precision computing, GPU performance optimization, and hardware-software co-design.


What you’ll be doing:

  • Analyze and optimize inference performance across model architecture, numerical precision, GPU kernels, memory systems, and end-to-end serving frameworks.
  • Develop low-bit quantization techniques for model weights, activations, attention operands, and KV caches.
  • Explore numerical formats and mixed-precision strategies involving FP8, NVFP4, MXFP4, and other emerging low-precision formats while preserving model accuracy and capabilities.
  • Design and evaluate techniques for KV cache compression, sparsification, hierarchical storage, and reuse across inference requests.
  • Optimize the inference of model architectures including MHA, GQA, MQA, MLA, sliding-window attention, sparse attention, linear attention, and state space models.
  • Investigate model-system co-optimization techniques such as speculative decoding, state reuse, and computation reuse.
  • Build performance models and optimization strategies for long-context inference and agentic workloads, with a focus on throughput, time to first token, inter-token latency, memory efficiency, and deployment cost.
  • Collaborate closely with model, framework, kernel, library, system software, and GPU architecture teams to influence the design of future models, software platforms, and hardware architectures.

What we need to see:

  • Pursuing an MS or PhD from a leading university in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related field, with an expected graduation date in 2028.
  • Available to work as an intern for at least three months and at least four days per week.
  • Strong understanding of Transformer architectures and large language model inference, including core components such as attention, MoE, and KV cache management.
  • Experience with at least one large language model inference framework, such as TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, SGLang, or a comparable framework.
  • Proficiency in Python and PyTorch, with strong experimental design, data analysis, debugging, and problem-solving skills.
  • Experience with at least one GPU programming technology, such as CUDA C/C++, Triton, or a comparable parallel programming framework.
  • Understanding of GPU architecture, memory hierarchy, Tensor Cores, parallel computing, and performance analysis.
  • Familiarity with low-precision computing concepts, including quantization error, scaling, rounding, clipping, group or block quantization, and mixed-precision computation.
  • Ability to evaluate an optimization technique across model accuracy, kernel performance, and end-to-end inference performance.
  • Good communication, technical writing, organization, and cross-functional collaboration skills.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Hands-on experience optimizing kernels or end-to-end workloads on NVIDIA GPUs.
  • Research or engineering experience in model quantization, KV cache optimization, efficient attention, speculative decoding, or long-context inference.
  • Contributions to inference frameworks, GPU libraries, compilers, or other relevant open-source projects.
  • Experience profiling and optimizing production-scale LLM inference workloads.

title: Agent Evaluation and Self-Improvement Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Autonomous agents now do real work across NVIDIA, and every piece underneath them keeps changing: models, harnesses, tools, skills, and plugins. Evaluation is how a team knows whether a change made an agent better or quietly made it worse. We're looking for a principal engineer to set evaluation strategy at every layer, from individual skills and MCP servers to whole agents and products, and to design how agents use those results to improve themselves.


Agents can already rewrite the skills and plugins they run on, then test whether the change helped. Making that loop trustworthy is the hard part. What does it take for an agent to get better on its own, and prove the improvement is real? We're building a system that answers that question for every agent at NVIDIA. Come build it with us!


What you'll be doing:

  • Build evaluation that works the same across harnesses, with automated checks on every change that catch regressions before users do.
  • Mine production traces for failures, new usage patterns, missing skills and tools, cost and latency hot spots, and successful runs. Turn them into eval cases and improvement signals.
  • Evaluate the eval datasets themselves: coverage of real usage, duplicate cases, and how closely they match production.
  • Build the self-improvement loop for evolving harnesses: agents propose changes to their own skills, plugins, and harness configuration, and sandboxed evals test each one. Only measurable gains ship, with human sign-off and limits agents can't change.
  • Create realistic enterprise environments: sandboxed replicas of issue trackers, code repositories, chat, and internal APIs, filled with synthetic or anonymized data, where agents safely run long, end-to-end tasks.
  • Measure multi-agent swarms as a team: how agents split work, whether handoffs succeed, and whether permissions hold at every hop. Record how long each task takes and how many tokens it uses.
  • Keep evals honest: calibrate model and agent judges against human labels. Catch agents that cheat, such as working backward from expected answers or reaching data and tools they shouldn't access. We work closely with product, platform, and hardware teams throughout NVIDIA, and we help shape open evaluation standards and benchmarks across the industry.

What we need to see:

  • BS or MS in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field (or equivalent experience)
  • 12+ years building large-scale systems, including evaluation systems for ML or agents and the data pipelines that feed them
  • Hands-on experience building and evaluating agents on an open or closed agent harness
  • Solid grounding in experiment design: statistical significance, variance across repeated runs, and A/B testing
  • Experience setting technical direction across teams as a senior individual contributor
  • Proficiency in Python, Go, Rust, or similar

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Built self-improving or self-evolving agent systems that get better from their own eval results
  • Shipped an agent benchmark, eval framework, or simulated test environment adopted by other teams
  • Detected reward hacking or eval gaming, or built oversight for systems that modify themselves
  • Built domain evaluations, such as for chip design or hardware verification

For over 25 years, NVIDIA has been at the forefront of transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing, driven by a legacy of continuous innovation and exceptional talent. We are now leveraging the immense potential of AI to usher in the next era of computing, where our GPUs power the "brains" of computers, robots, and autonomous vehicles that can comprehend the world. This pioneering work demands vision, innovation, and the world's best talent. Join our diverse and supportive environment, where NVIDIANs are inspired to excel and make a profound global impact.


We're hiring an engineer to own the engineering efforts across NVIDIA enterprise systems. You'll partner with IT leadership to transform reactive support into strategic, AI infused automated resolution systems and prevent problems before they occur, balancing speed, security, and an exceptional user experience for NVIDIAs.


What You’ll Be Doing:

  • Design and implement agentic AI workflows using LLM-based agents, tool calling, RAG patterns, and orchestration frameworks. Push the boundaries of what AI-assisted operations can achieve.
  • Build robust integrations and automation pipelines across ServiceNow, identity management, monitoring platforms, and enterprise SaaS. Own the full stack from infrastructure to user facing tools.
  • Triage and resolve Enterprise issues with a focus on automation and improving mitigation and resolution times
  • Manage and troubleshoot Enterprise scale collaboration, productivity, AI and Infrastructure systems.
  • Trace and root cause complex, multi system failures. identify patterns in recurring tickets, and build automation or self-service solutions
  • Build and maintain runbooks, troubleshooting guides, and knowledge base articles that elevate team capabilities
  • Mentor team members on troubleshooting methodology and systems thinking

What We Need To See:

  • Bachelors Degree or equivalent experience
  • 8+ years in SRE, Enterprise Support or Devops, Experience with SaaS, hybrid cloud, AI/ML environments
  • Experience building production grade agentic workflows (e.g., multi-agent systems and MCP servers)
  • Software engineering fundamentals with deep experience in building products and operating large scale systems.
Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and other objective job-related factors. The expected base salary range for this position is 168,000 USD – 270,250 USD.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

Applications for this job will be accepted at least until November 6, 2026.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

title: System Software Engineer Intern, Autonomous Vehicles - 2027
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA is the engine of the AI era. We invented the GPU, and the accelerated computing it made possible now powers the world's most advanced AI, from the data center to the car. Today, NVIDIA DRIVE brings that intelligence to the road: a full-stack platform that lets vehicles perceive, reason and act in the real world. We are looking to grow our teams with the smartest people in the world, and there has never been a more exciting time to join us.


The Autonomous Vehicles team develops and ships NVIDIA's DRIVE software platform. Our AV Stability group owns the reliability of the full stack on real vehicles: every issue found on a test drive flows through us before it reaches the owning team. You will reproduce, investigate and help fix the problems that stand between a prototype and a product, working with sensor, perception, planning and platform teams across the globe. As AI reshapes how engineering itself is done, our team is also where that change meets the vehicle: we increasingly build intelligent tooling on top of the same expertise we use to debug the car. We have real customers and real competition, and the work is exciting, fun, and very meaningful.


What you'll be doing:


  • Use in-house data playback, simulation, and visualization tools to re-animate and reproduce performance issues experienced during test drives.
  • Collaborate with software and algorithm experts to investigate, deduce, and isolate root causes of test drive issues, and to develop fixes and improvements.
  • Design and implement Autonomous Vehicles software, including system integration, application design, performance/power optimization, and stress/stability/compliance testing.
  • Drive the reliability of the whole software system, including time sync, vehicle network, RADAR, LiDAR, and camera sensor processing, and fusion.
  • Help turn hard-won debugging expertise into tooling and automation, including AI-assisted analysis of logs and vehicle data, so that problems are found faster and recur less.
  • Develop a strong technical understanding of the stack, and proactively identify new opportunities and creative ways to solve or mitigate technical challenges.

What we need to see:


  • Pursuing a BS or MS in CS/CE/EE/Robotics or a related field.
  • Demonstrated proficiency in both C/C++ and Python: C/C++ to understand and debug the vehicle software stack, Python to build the tooling around it.
  • Strong debugging instincts: you can read logs and traces, form a hypothesis, and prove or disprove it with evidence.
  • Ability of using modern AI coding assistants as part of your everyday workflow, while verifying what they produce.
  • Familiar with git or other version control tooling.
  • Ability and flexibility to work and communicate effectively in a multinational, multi-time-zone environment.
  • Self-motivated and a good teammate.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:


  • Good knowledge of key Autonomous Driving technologies and the typical challenges of key components; prior experience in the AV field.
  • Worked with CAN and related tools, RADAR, LiDAR.
  • Hands-on experience with LLM-based tooling: prompt and context design, tool calling, agent workflows, or evaluation of model output on a real task.
  • Experience with large-scale log analysis and cloud-based workflows.

title: Senior Package Layout Engineer - Hardware
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA has continuously reinvented itself. Our invention of the GPU sparked the growth of the PC gaming market, redefined modern computer graphics, and revolutionized parallel computing. Today, research in artificial intelligence is booming worldwide, which calls for highly scalable and massively parallel computation horsepower that NVIDIA GPUs excel. NVIDIA is a “learning machine” that constantly evolves by adapting to new opportunities that are hard to solve, that only we can address, and that matter to the world. This is our life’s work , to amplify human creativity and intelligence. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in a diverse, supportive environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join our diverse team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world!

NVIDIA's GPUs and SOCs are the world leaders in power, performance and efficiency. We are continually innovating to deliver new and creative, unusual solutions to extraordinary problems in a wide range of sectors. To this purpose, we are now seeking a hard-working Senior Package Layout Engineer who is committed to making a difference in the world through their contributions! This position will collaborate with Technical Package Lead and different design teams in the design and development of sophisticated, detailed layout of IC substrates for NVIDIA products. In addition, work with design teams to plan schedules, resolve costs, manufacturing, and electrical design issues.


What you'll be doing:

  • As part of a Layout team, you will collaborate to implement high speed/density ASIC packages.

  • Perform substrate breakout patterns for ASIC packages.

  • Optimize package pinout incorporating system level trade-offs of pins assignment.

  • Help perform package routing, placement, stack-up, reference plane and power distribution using Cadence APD or SiP tool suite.

  • Propose layout design trade-offs to the Technical Package Lead for resolution and implementation.

  • Conduct design feasibility studies to evaluate the Package design goals for size, cost, and system performance.

  • Develop symbols and CAD library databases using Cadence APD design tools

  • Develop methodologies to improve layout productivity


What we need to see:

  • Hold a B.S. Electrical Engineering or equivalent experience

  • 5+ years experience in PCB Layout of graphics cards, motherboards, line cards or other related technology. Experience with HDI designs is a plus

  • Proven experience in substrate layout of wire bond and flip chip packages, preferred

  • Significant background with Cadence APD or SiP and/or PCB layout tools (including Constraint Manager)

  • Solid understanding of high-speed design signal integrity practices

  • Experience with Virtuoso and Calibre is a plus

  • Experience using Valor is helpful
     

NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers! We have some of the most forward-thinking and dedicated people in the world working for us. If you're creative and autonomous, we want to hear from you.

title: Senior Manager, Training Data
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA is seeking a senior product leader to define the strategy and build the platforms that deliver high-quality training data for our foundation models. Starting with web and code data for Nemotron, you will help research teams discover valuable new sources from the open web, improve data quality and diversity, and turn raw content into datasets that advance model capabilities. In this founding product leadership role, you will partner with an engineering lead and work across research, data acquisition, data platforms, and legal teams to build the roadmap and investment priorities. You will connect data acquisition and curation decisions to measurable training outcomes, balancing quality, scale, delivery time, and cost. As research needs evolve, you will extend the platform to additional domains and modalities!


This role offers the opportunity to shape a foundational capability for NVIDIA’s AI models, working directly with researchers and engineers to improve what our models can learn. If you bring deep technical curiosity, product judgment, and a record of delivering ambitious data platforms, we want to hear from you.


What you’ll be doing:

  • Own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for training data acquisition and preparation. Translate research priorities and model capability gaps into source requirements, platform investments, and dataset acceptance criteria aligned with training schedules.
  • Define requirements for source discovery, URL indexing, predictive quality and diversity ranking, crawl scheduling, distributed fetching, and ingestion. Partner with engineering on throughput, reliability, storage, and capacity planning as workloads scale.
  • Drive improvements in parsing and curation, including HTML extraction, browser-rendered content, code and math preservation, duplication, quality filtering, and dataset composition. Identify where valuable content is lost and increase the yield of usable, differentiated data.
  • Lead build, buy, and partner decisions across internal crawling, commercial datasets, and licensed content. Establish comparable internal and vendor pilots that measure incremental coverage, accepted data yield, delivery reliability, and total cost against existing corpora.
  • Partner with researchers on controlled training experiments and ablations to measure data impact on model capabilities. Account for benchmark contamination, dataset composition, and regressions, and use results to guide source selection and acquisition investment.
  • Work with legal, privacy, policy, and security teams to translate approved requirements into scalable controls for source eligibility, access restrictions, opt-outs, provenance, and permitted use. Define auditable dataset acceptance and release processes.
  • Build researcher-facing capabilities for dataset discovery, metadata, versioning, lineage, and quality reporting. Enable reproducible dataset releases and reuse, measure adoption, and reduce the time from a research request to training-ready data.
  • Align teams on priorities, dependencies, and ownership. Shape hiring and resource plans with engineering leadership, communicate investment tradeoffs to senior leaders, and establish shared metrics for model impact, data coverage, pipeline latency, cost, and delivery against training cutoffs.

What we need to see:

  • A BS or MS in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience.
  • 8+ overall years in product management or a related technical role, including 5+ years on data platforms, search/indexing, or ML infrastructure.
  • 4+ years direct people management experience
  • A track record of delivering data systems at scale and improving quality, reliability, processing time, adoption, or cost. Experience building a new platform or taking a technically complex product from concept to production.
  • Strong technical understanding of distributed data pipelines, storage, indexing or retrieval, and data processing. Ability to engage in architecture and capacity discussions and make informed product tradeoffs with engineers.
  • Experience working closely with research or ML teams to turn evolving needs into datasets or platform capabilities. Good judgment in experiment design, baseline selection, and distinguishing data quality proxies from proven model improvement.
  • Strong analytical skills and the ability to inspect data and performance metrics using SQL, Python, or equivalent tools. Comfort making decisions with incomplete information and refining priorities as evidence develops.
  • Clear written and verbal communication, with proven ability to influence engineering, research, legal, and commercial stakeholders and secure decisions on scope, resources, and investment.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Direct experience with foundation-model training data, large-scale web crawling, source discovery, HTML parsing, or corpus curation.
  • Experience evaluating data suppliers, integrating publisher content, defining licensing requirements, or optimizing data acquisition economics.
  • Background with code, mathematical, multilingual, or multimodal datasets, semantic discovery, and quality ranking systems.
  • Experience establishing a product function, mentoring product managers, and shaping teams in partnership with engineering leaders.
  • Familiarity with synthetic data, reinforcement-learning environments, or post-training data workflows.

NVIDIA is widely considered one of the technology world’s most desirable employers. We have some of the world's most forward-thinking and hardworking people on our team. If you're creative and autonomous, we want to hear from you!

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and other objective job-related factors. The expected base salary range for this position is 240,000 USD – 379,500 USD.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

title: Senior Infrastructure Security Engineer – EDA Clusters
descriptionHtml:
Securing NVIDIA's EDA clusters is not a matter of deploying a standard security stack. The workloads are too large, too long-running, and too performance-sensitive for an off-the-shelf playbook to simply apply. That constraint is the job. You'll be an individual contributor on Infrastructure Security Engineering for EDA Clusters, the team that implements security controls across the compute, storage, and networking that NVIDIA's hardware engineers design silicon on - spanning on-prem data centers and multi-cloud. You will sit alongside the engineers who run these clusters 24x7, close enough to deploy a control, investigate a behavior, and change the running environment yourself.


This is hands-on build work, not control review. You'll decide where conventional tooling applies, where it actively cannot, and then engineer the alternative. If your depth is in large-scale compute, networking, or storage infrastructure at a hyperscaler, a security product company, or anywhere fleets and fabrics are the day job, and you've carried real accountability for the security properties of those systems, you're who we want to talk to. We don't expect fluency in every security product category. We expect you to own outcomes and pick up the remaining domain breadth fast. Security engineering here is engineering: code, instrumentation, and secure-by-default infrastructure - not tickets, exceptions, and spreadsheets.


What You'll Be Doing:

  • Build and operate security controls and telemetry for EDA compute, storage, and networking - design, ship to production, then own them.
  • Engineer around hard constraints. Protect multi-day, high-value compute jobs without degrading them. Where heavyweight in-node agents are not viable, build the workable answer instead.
  • Make the network and platform the control plane. Protection can't depend solely on what runs inside the node.
  • Instrument for detection. Collect and normalize security signals from the fleet into our SIEM, and build the detections and dashboards that turn it into something actionable. Log collection alone is not monitoring.
  • Investigate and respond. Chase down EDA-specific threats and exposure, and execute containment and remediation hands-on with infrastructure and service owners.
  • Automate enforcement and evidence. Infrastructure-as-code and policy-as-code so secure configuration is the default state, with compliance evidence produced as an engineering output rather than a manual exercise.
  • Run the lifecycle of the security technologies you own: selection, rollout, operation, and eventual replacement.
  • Work across boundaries. Partner directly with data center operations, IT storage and networking, network engineering, CSP teams, and NVIDIA's central security organization on shared outcomes.
  • Think like an adversary. Threat modeling and mitigation planning across network, storage, and compute.

What We Need To See:

  • 8+ years of hands-on infrastructure or infrastructure-security engineering across on-prem and cloud environments.
  • Strong Linux depth - you are comfortable at the system level, not just the console level.
  • Real experience operating or securing compute fleets at scale: provisioning, lifecycle, and the operational realities of long-running jobs.
  • Working networking expertise applied to large compute environments.
  • Programming/scripting fluency (Python, Go, or shell) used for automation, detection, and tooling you've shipped and maintained.
  • Solid foundations in access control, authentication, segmentation, encryption, and vulnerability lifecycle.
  • A track record of landing changes with partners who don't report to you.
  • Clear written and verbal communication - credible with individual engineers and with leadership.
  • A Bachelor's degree in a relevant engineering field or equivalent experience.

Ways To Stand Out from the Crowd:

  • Security or platform engineering inside EDA, HPC, or large research-cluster environments.
  • Breadth across security domains - IAM, EDR/XDR, CNAPP, CSPM, zero-trust architectures - or a demonstrated pattern of picking up new domains fast.
  • Built or operated infrastructure security capabilities at a hyperscaler or a security product company - you engineered detection and enforcement systems rather than deploying someone else's.
  • Experience with kernel- and fabric-level observability and enforcement - eBPF, in-line and out-of-band inspection, DPU/SmartNIC offload - as an alternative to heavyweight in-node agents.
  • Contributions to open-source security or infrastructure tooling.

Widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers, NVIDIA offers highly competitive salaries and a comprehensive benefits package. We have some of the most forward-thinking and talented people in the world working for us and, due to outstanding growth, our world-class engineering teams are growing fast. If you're a creative and autonomous engineer with real passion for technology, we want to hear from you.

title: Manufacturing Automation Solution Intern - 2027
descriptionHtml:
We are excited to offer an outstanding opportunity for a Manufacturing Automation Solution Intern - 2027 to join our world-class team at NVIDIA! This role is perfect for an ambitious individual looking to make a significant impact in the field of industrial automation and Physical AI.


This role involves leading efforts in industrial automation and Physical AI with Omniverse by NVIDIA and OpenUSD frameworks. You will transform complex physical automation equipment, test cells, and robotic systems into accurate digital twins. You will collaborate with mechanical, test, and software groups to develop the future of industrial production based on Omniverse. If you are enthusiastic about 3D graphics, physics simulation, robotics, and bringing code to life with kinetic motion, this role is an excellent platform to begin your career.


What you will be doing:

  • Clean up, lightweight, and render industrial CAD models into the NVIDIA Omniverse platform, building standardized, high-fidelity OpenUSD 3D digital assets.
  • Define OpenUSD asset standards (scene hierarchy, PhysX materials, semantic schemas) for automated equipment in Omniverse, opening them to ecosystem partners to build a unified asset ecosystem.
  • Establish virtual testing and interference review standards in Omniverse; evaluate facility footprint and maintenance limits, directing vendors to deliver compliant scenes and equipment models within Omniverse.
  • Formulate simulation and Cycle Time (CT) demo examples and evaluation standards for axis/robotics in NVIDIA Isaac Sim / PhysX. This drives vendors to improve CT and remove efficiency bottlenecks virtually in Omniverse.
  • Define communication interface standards (OPC UA/Modbus) using Omniverse Python APIs. Connect the equipment software platform with controllers. Guide vendors to plug into Omniverse for Software-in-the-Loop (SIL) commissioning.
  • Build digital twin reference implementations by ingesting real-time sensor and machine telemetry data into NVIDIA Omniverse. Establish standardized technical frameworks and API guidelines to empower and guide vendors in replicating live 3D sync and supervising across their own equipment.
  • Fully bring to bear NVIDIA Omniverse technologies and ecosystem capabilities to translate Physical AI into real-world industrial efficiency, exploring emerging business models for digital twins in automation.

What we need to see:

  • Currently pursuing a degree (BS or MS) in Computer Science, Automation, Robotics, Mechatronics, Software Engineering, or a related technical domain.
  • Strong Python programming skills (Required; ability to write clean, object-oriented scripts and APIs). Familiarity with Linux environments and common industrial communication protocols (e.g., OPC UA, Modbus, TCP/IP) is preferred.
  • Practical experience with at least one 3D simulation or game engine (e.g., NVIDIA Omniverse, Isaac Sim, Unreal Engine, Unity) or 3D CAD software (SolidWorks, Creo, NX, Blender, etc.).
  • Excellent analytical problem-solving skills; strong cross-functional communication approach to collaborate effectively with mechanical engineers, omniverse developers, and third-party equipment vendors.
  • Skilled in both Chinese and English, capable of independently guiding and engaging in technical business discussions in English.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Practical experience working directly with NVIDIA Omniverse and its essential ecosystem components, including Isaac Sim (robotics & automation simulation).
  • Familiarity with Pixar OpenUSD structures is a strong plus.
  • Familiarity with industrial control software or automation equipment software is preferred.
  • Practical project experience in software/hardware communication setup via OPC UA, Modbus-TCP, MQTT, or WebSockets; familiarity with Software-in-the-Loop (SIL) virtual commissioning workflows.
  • Strong engineering standardization approach with the ability to distill reference implementations from practical projects. Write structured API documentation and standard specifications. Empower external vendors and ecosystem partners.

Join us at NVIDIA and help build the future of industrial automation with innovative technology!

title: Senior Software Engineer, AV Analysis Platform
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA is seeking a senior software engineer to help build and scale evaluation and analysis infrastructure for Autonomous Vehicle development. This role sits at the intersection of AV tooling, distributed systems, data platforms, and developer efficiency. You will develop and enhance systems that allow AV engineers to run AV log data analysis, assess model behavior, debug regressions, and produce critical metrics and insights at scale.


This engineer should be able to operate independently, partner deeply with senior technical leads, and bring clarity to complex platform decisions spanning evaluator execution at high-scale, performance tunings, structured outputs and output schema evolution, observability, and production readiness. This role directly improves how AV engineers examine autonomous driving performance, analyze regressions, validate analyzers, and trust the results produced by NVIDIA’s AV infrastructure. The ideal candidate will help make evaluation workflows faster, safer, more observable, and easier for teams to adopt.


What you'll be doing:

  • Design and build evaluation and analysis tooling used by AV and ML engineers.
  • Improve analyzer workflows, including onboarding, execution, qualification, and production observability.

title: Principal Engineer, Package Integration and Manufacturability
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. It’s a unique legacy of innovation that’s fueled by great technology—and amazing people. Today, we’re tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in an inclusive, supportive environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world.


NVIDIA is a fast-growing world leader supporting the most powerful supercomputers worldwide. Our networking products lead the industry and connect thousands of GPUs. We make outstanding artificial intelligence possible through innovative networking and computing integration. We value our people and seek excellent individuals to join us! We are looking for an experienced packaging, technology and manufacturability expert to help us build the next generation of networking products. Our networking devices depend heavily on advanced packaging methods like chiplet integration, 2.5D interposers, and co-packaged optics. Packaging choices influence schedule, cost, and yield equally with the silicon. We are looking for a packaging and manufacturability lead who will own the package technical view across our chip programs. This role partners with the advanced technology group to push technology limits in future products. Joining an outstanding team, you will highlight package risks early, bring manufacturability into design choices before they are fixed, and find co-design approaches that improve module yield. Join us in making an impact on all networking products and pushing the boundaries of technology.


What you’ll be doing:

  • Lead the technical assessment of package risk across our chip programs — identifying failure modes in substrate, interposer and assembly integration before they reach silicon, quantifying their cost and schedule impact, and bringing them to program and technology reviews with a clear position
  • Drive new approaches to manufacturability across the board (package, substrate, interposer, silicon), spanning yield improvement, capacity and supply review, test strategy, thermal and assembly process maturity. Push co-design levers such as tolerance relaxation by design, testability before attach, design margins, and redundancy and partial-module recovery
  • Analyze module yield mechanics, reconcile predicted versus actual yield on units returning from assembly, and convert the findings into concrete design guidance
  • Evaluate emerging packaging and photonics technologies, including outside partner solutions, and define our product requirements — working closely with our advanced technology group

What we need to see:

  • B.S or M.S. in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Materials Science or equivalent experience
  • More than 15 years of experience in package technology development or system integration, with multiple products carried through assembly
  • Deep understanding of 2.5D, chiplet and organic substrate integration. Working knowledge of assembly and module yield mechanics, including how alignment tolerance and process excursions drive assembly yield differently from defect density at the die level
  • Strong analytic capabilities, and passion for solving demanding technical problems
  • Ability to drive complex activities involving many interfaces and teams, and to hold a technical position across organizations

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Hands-on experience on an assembly floor, a foundry or at an OSAT
  • Experience with co-packaged optics, photonic packaging, or fiber and laser attach
  • Proven experience driving design-for-manufacturability into early architecture decisions
  • Familiar with working on large high-end ASICs and multi-die modules

descriptionHtml:

Your primary focus will be adapting NVIDIA software to vehicle platforms, diagnosing system-level issues and validating parking behavior in development and production vehicles. You will work across perception, fusion, environment modeling, and vehicle integration to trace problems through the full parking chain, identify root causes, implement or coordinate appropriate solutions, and turn findings into actionable input for NVIDIA engineering teams.

  • Configure and tune parking software for different vehicle platforms, sensor configurations, vehicle geometries, and low-speed maneuvering requirements.
  • Debug fusion and environment-modeling behavior that combines sensor and neural-network outputs into a consistent and temporally stable representation of the vehicle surroundings.
  • Implement targeted C++ or Python adaptations, debugging tools, and analysis workflows where needed to resolve customer integration and functional issues.
  • Measure functional performance through recorded-data replay and in-vehicle testing, and communicate findings clearly to customers and NVIDIA engineering teams.

What we need to see:

title: Research Intern, Robotics - 2027
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA Research is seeking research interns in Singapore to advance fundamental and applied robotics research, with a particular focus on agentic robotics.

We are interested in exploring how AI agents can autonomously develop, refine, and generalize robotic capabilities by integrating reasoning, programming, experimentation, and feedback within the full robot systems stack. Our research spans robot learning, planning, simulation, perception, and control, with an emphasis on building intelligent systems that can generalize over tasks, environments, and embodiments.

We are looking for interns with strong research and engineering skills, intellectual curiosity, and a collaborative mindset. You will have the opportunity to formulate and pursue ambitious research questions, develop novel algorithms and systems, and validate your ideas through rigorous experimentation. Research projects will be aligned with your expertise and the team's priorities, with opportunities to contribute to scientific publications and practical robotic systems.


What you will be doing

* Conduct research on novel models, algorithms, and systems for agentic robotics.

* Investigate how AI agents can autonomously develop, evaluate, and improve robotic programs and capabilities.

* Explore research directions at the intersection of foundation models, robot learning, planning, and programming.

* Develop and evaluate methods for robotic skill acquisition, adaptation, and generalization.

* Design and conduct experiments in simulation and, where appropriate, on physical robots.

* Collaborate with researchers and engineers across robotics and AI, and communicate research outcomes through publications, demonstrations, open-source contributions, and presentation.


What we need to see

* Currently pursuing a PhD in robotics,  artificial intelligence, computer science, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, or a related field.

* Strong technical foundation in robotics, AI, or related areas, with an interest in real-world robotic systems.

* Demonstrated ability to conduct independent research, evidenced by publications, impactful projects, or substantial research contributions.

* Strong programming skills and experience in developing research software.

* Ability to formulate research questions, implement novel methods, and rigorously evaluate experimental results.

* Excellent problem-solving, communication, and collaboration skills.


Ways to stand out from the crowd

* Research experience in AI coding agents, robotics, foundation models, or program synthesis.

* Expertise in one or more areas such as robot learning, planning, simulation, perception, control, ...

* Familiarity with robotics and simulation platforms such as ROS 2, Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab, or MuJoCo.

* Experience implementing and validating methods on real robotic systems.

* Publications at leading robotics conferences and journals, such as RSS, CoRL, ICRA, IROS, T-RO, IJRR, or RA-L.

Join NVIDIA Research to explore how AI agents can transform robotics research and industry.

descriptionHtml:

In this role, you will lead and manage a cluster of IP teams responsible for both design and design verification (DV) of complex hardware IP blocks across NVIDIA’s next-generation SmartNIC and DPU products. You will own the end-to-end delivery of IPs — from micro-architecture definition and RTL implementation through functional verification, lint/CDC/RDC closure, synthesis, and silicon readiness.


We are looking for someone who thrives on building high-performing teams, driving IP execution across multiple parallel projects, and partnering with architecture, SoC integration, physical design, software, and program management teams to deliver world-class silicon.


What You’ll Be Doing:

  • Lead, mentor, and grow a team of design and verification engineers across a cluster of IP blocks. You will define team structure, hiring plans, and career development paths to build a strong, scalable organization.
  • Own the end-to-end execution of IP delivery — micro-architecture, RTL design, functional verification, coverage closure, assertions, formal verification, and synthesis handoff. You will set quality bars, review schedules, and drive milestone adherence across your IP cluster.
  • Define and drive verification strategies, test plans, coverage goals, and sign-off criteria for your IPs. Your team will develop UVM-based constrained-random and directed test environments, achieve functional and code coverage targets, and ensure robust regression infrastructure.
  • Partner with architecture, SoC integration, physical design, DFT, firmware, and software teams to resolve cross-functional dependencies, close interface specifications, and ensure seamless IP integration. We will look to you to identify risks early, drive trade-off decisions, and align technical priorities across stakeholders.

title: Senior Mixed Signal Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA has continuously reinvented itself over two decades. Our invention of the GPU in 1999 sparked the growth of the PC gaming market, redefined modern computer graphics, and revolutionized parallel computing. More recently, GPU deep learning ignited modern AI — the next era of computing. NVIDIA is a “learning machine” that constantly evolves by adapting to new opportunities that are hard to solve, that only we can tackle, and that matter to the world. This is our life’s work, to amplify human creativity and intelligence. Make the choice and join us today!


This is a dynamic team working with state of the art, unique technology. If you are someone that loves a challenge, come join this diverse team and help move the needle! We are looking for a senior engineer to be part of the mixed-signal design team building next generation NVLINK. This position offers the opportunity to have real impact in a dynamic, technology-focused company impacting product lines ranging from consumer graphics to self-driving cars and the growing field of artificial intelligence.


What you'll be doing:

  • CMOS Analog / Mixed Signal Circuit Design Experience in deep sub-micron process (especially in FINFET)
  • Experience with design and verification tools (Cadence's IC design environment, analog circuit simulation tools like Spectre, HSpice, Finesim, XA)
  • Experience in crafting test bench environments for component and top level circuit verification
  • Behavioral modeling of analog and digital circuits
  • Strong debugging and analytical skills

title: Senior Solutions Architect, DL Training
descriptionHtml:

Join us in this exciting endeavor!

  • Work with Cloud Service Providers to design, build, and demonstrate scalable AI training solutions using NVIDIA hardware and software.
  • Lead technical engagements across foundation model pre-training and post-training, helping customers move from architecture and proofs of concept to production adoption.
  • Develop and optimize end-to-end training workflows spanning data preparation, distributed training, checkpointing, and evaluation, including reinforcement learning pipelines.
  • Build customer-specific proofs of concept that address critical technical and business needs, demonstrating improvements in training performance, reliability, and efficiency.
  • Help customers diagnose and resolve bottlenecks across GPU compute, memory, communication, networking, storage, and workload orchestration.

title: Senior AI Systems and Algorithms Engineer
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA is seeking a Senior GenAI Algorithms Engineer to advance the state of the art in foundation model development, training, and deployment. You will work at the intersection of large-scale distributed training, reinforcement learning for LLMs/VLMs, model efficiency, multimodal AI, and open-source AI infrastructure. This role spans the entire GenAI lifecycle from large-scale data preparation to training, post-training, inference optimization, and framework development. You will collaborate with research, product, and infrastructure teams to design new algorithms, optimize existing systems, and contribute to NVIDIA's open-source AI stack, including Megatron-LM, Megatron Bridge, and NeMo-RL.


What You'll Be Doing:

  • Data Curation & Readiness: Design scalable systems for preparing high-quality multimodal datasets for frontier foundation model training.
  • Training Efficiency: Develop algorithms and systems that improve the scalability, efficiency, and cost of large-scale pre-training and post-training.
  • Inference Efficiency: Advance techniques that improve inference performance, reduce deployment cost, and enable efficient serving across cloud and edge platforms.
  • Open-Source AI Infrastructure: Develop reusable infrastructure and contribute brand new model support to NVIDIA's open-source GenAI training platform.

What We Need to See:

  • MS or Ph.D in Computer Science, AI, Applied Mathematics, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
  • 5+ years of relevant industry experience.
  • Strong foundation in machine learning, deep learning, and optimization.
  • Excellent software engineering skills, including Python and PyTorch.
  • Experience building high-performance software for large-scale AI systems.
  • Strong analytical, debugging, and performance optimization skills.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

Experience in some of the following areas is highly desirable:

  • Distributed training at scale using frameworks like Megatron-LM and Megatron Bridge. It includes FSDP, TP/PP/CP/DP, heterogeneous or per-module parallelism, optimizer research, and efficient sparse or long-context attention.
  • LLM/VLM Post-Training: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT), reinforcement learning for LLMs (e.g., PPO, GRPO, asynchronous RL), and large-scale RL frameworks such as NeMo-RL.
  • Inference Efficiency: Model compression techniques including quantization (FP8, NVFP4, INT4), pruning, knowledge distillation, neural architecture search, and diffusion or non-autoregressive language models.
  • Open-Source AI Infrastructure: Contributing to open-source AI frameworks such as Megatron-LM, Megatron Bridge, NeMo-RL, or Hugging Face Transformers along with experience in GPU performance optimization, distributed systems, latency/throughput analysis, and profiling of large-scale AI workloads.

title: Software Engineer, Technical Lead – Performance Data Platform
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. It’s a unique legacy of innovation that’s fueled by great technology—and amazing people. Today, we’re tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in an inclusive, supportive environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world.


NVIDIA wants a technical lead to invent a new platform that enables engineers to assess the performance of AI workloads running on numerous computing nodes. Our team develops software tools for technical users to comprehend complex computing systems. You will lead the architecture of a system that collects performance data at a data center scale, maintains it as searchable history, and permits both people and automated analysis agents to find and explain performance issues. You will evolve this from an early prototype into a product used by other teams, while building hands-on as the team expands.


What you’ll be doing:

  • Define the end-to-end architecture: the data model, the service and API contracts, and the boundaries with the tools and teams that produce the data.
  • Make foundational decisions and justify them in documents. Include considered alternatives and evidence that could reverse them. Align these decisions with partner teams and their roadmaps.
  • Build in the early phase: stand up services, APIs and a deployment path yourself, so that partners can develop the system before every role is filled.
  • Explain how automated analysis agents operate within the platform. Describe what queries they may perform, how their results relate to evidence, and the constraints on their cost and response time.
  • Review performance diagnoses and drive the first use cases with design partners, mentor engineers, and establish the engineering approaches the team grows into.

What we need to see:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • 15+ years of software engineering experience, including technical leadership of a data-intensive platform that shipped end to end and was used by other teams.
  • Experience developing or managing systems where automated agents or models process large amounts of production data, including methods used to assess the quality of their results.
  • Practical knowledge of GPU and machine learning workload performance: you can review a performance diagnosis, question its evidence, and decide which signals matter most.
  • A track record of crafting APIs and data models that evolved without breaking existing users or deployments.
  • Hands-on ability to build and deploy services and tooling yourself, including when using automated development tools, and to verify the result independently through tests and measurements.
  • Clear communication of build choices, trade-offs and uncertainty to engineers, partner teams and leadership, and the ability to align teams without direct authority.
  • Proficiency with C++, Go, Python.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Background in developer tools, profilers or performance-analysis products.
  • Experience transforming a prototype into a platform embraced by multiple teams with distinct priorities.
  • Identity, access control and multi-tenant build for products that hold customers’ data.
  • Evaluation approach for the output of analysis agents or models: labeled cases, precision and recall, abstention.
  • Working knowledge of SQL and TypeScript.

Join NVIDIA and be part of a team that’s redefining what’s possible through technology. Together, we’ll build a platform that sets new standards for performance data analysis and empowers engineers worldwide to achieve flawless results!

title: Circuit Validation Engineer - New College Graduate 2027
descriptionHtml:
Silicon Co-Design Group (SCG) is a wide-ranging, multi-functional, integral team at NVIDIA. We sit at the crossroads of design, architecture, marketing, operations, and productization. Our contributions span from the arch stage and extend to defining final products. We architect innovative solutions for Datacenter, Server, Gaming, Robotics, Automotive, and Embedded markets. We are fast-paced, dynamic, share a sense of humor, and collaborate extensively to push the boundaries of what is possible. We do all of this with an eye on making groundbreaking, impactful market disruptions! We are looking for a Circuit Validation Engineer(NCG) to define and validate circuit methodologies across GPUs and SoCs, validate circuit behavior, performance, quality, and product readiness. This is a highly visible, multi-functional role focused on building methodologies that help products meet SOL(Speed Of Light) milestones and achieve the high NVIDIA quality bar our customers expect.

What you will be doing:

  • Standing up silicon co-design prototypes and measurement setups that expose power-rail noise, circuit enablement and tuning, performance, and volume behavior — from first bring-up through repeatable experiments that others can rerun.
  • Planning and executing design of experiments (DOE): choosing factors and ranges (voltage, frequency, workload, temperature, process), defining sample plans and success criteria, and analyzing main effects and interactions so results are usable, not just collected.
  • Building Python pipelines and analyses that turn prototype, DOE, simulation, and characterization data (power, noise, Vmin/Fmax, binning yield) into traces, summaries, and inputs for firmware tuning, product specs, and manufacturing limits — with checks for schema, units, corners, and SKU mapping.
  • Partnering with architecture, design, validation, and firmware to add debug hooks, iterate the prototype, and document what the experiment proved versus what still needs silicon char
  • Using secure, traceable, validated AI-assisted workflows for experiment planning, analysis, and documentation, with human oversight on any conclusion that could affect limits, bins, or specs.

What we need to see:

  • MS in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.
  • Background in a related silicon, validation, characterization, productization (SoC, GPU, CPU, or similar).
  • Working knowledge of silicon circuit/clock/power/noise concepts — for example DVFS, Vmin/Fmax, shmoo, PDN/noise, Driver, or margins — and comfort with learning DOE and prototype bring-up in a co-design setting.
  • Hands-on experience with at least one of: lab or post-silicon bring-up, experiment or characterization campaigns or manufacturing test/limits that consume chip data.
  • Proficiency in Python (or similar) for data analysis, automation, and validation; comfort with Git and structured test/regression. SQL or lightweight dashboards are a plus.
  • Ability to turn an ambiguous silicon question into a measurable experiment, communicate clearly across teams, and write notes others can execute from.
  • Strong AI-enabled skills and thinking — use AI to accelerate analysis, exploration, and documentation while maintaining rigor, originality, and judgment that do not come from AI.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • You have run a test-chip, prototype vehicle, or characterization DOE and can explain what you would change in the next matrix.
  • Direct experience on GPU/SoC/CPU circuits, power, performance, PDN/noise, or sim-to-silicon correlation.
  • You have shipped an internal tool, dashboard, or data pipeline (Python, databases, web apps) that other people actually use.
  • Hands-on LLMs in an engineering workflow — agents, RAG, or evaluation — including a time you had to debug a incorrect or unsafe answer.
  • Exposure to firmware/BIOS parameters, eFuse/limits, or ATE/SLT screening, and how they connect to product SKUs.

NVIDIA is a “learning machine” that constantly evolves by adapting to new opportunities that are hard to take on, that only we can pursue, and that matter to the world. This is our life’s work, to amplify human creativity and intelligence. We would love to hear from you!

title: Senior CPU Architect

To operationalize these automated workflows, you will partner with Research and Model Development teams thereby delivering novel models for harm detection, content moderation, dynamic guardrails, post-training, and groundbreaking automated research pipelines that push the limits. This role is built for a tenacious builder and an inquisitive problem solver. We want an engineer who thrives in ambiguity. They must have the grit to overcome complex technical challenges and transform innovative safety concepts from raw ideas to scalable implementations.


What You’ll Be Doing:

  • Architect Agentic Automation: Compose, build, and deploy foundational agentic automation loops that streamline workflows spanning safety evaluations, red-teaming, model testing, model post-training and ablations.
  • Develop Safety Models: Move from infrastructure automation towards training and implementing specialized systems for identifying harmful content, coordinating content quality, and run-time guard-railing.
  • Pioneer Auto-Research: Build and guide automated research frameworks. These frameworks use LLMs and autonomous agents to discover new vulnerabilities. They also generate or augment safety datasets for benchmarking or training and propose novel alignment techniques.
  • Scale Innovations: Take proof-of-concept safety interventions and research ideas and engineer them into robust, highly scalable solutions that integrate seamlessly into our production pipelines.
