  • Education: Bachelor’s degree or Master’s degree with equivalent experience in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Software Engineering, or a related field. 
  • Experience: Candidates should have a strong track record in ML engineering or software engineering with 8+ years of experience.
  • Agentic Systems & Automation: Proven experience building complex, automated workflows using LLMs, including multi-turn tool-calling, orchestration, and autonomous agent loops.
  • Strong engineering fundamentals include deep proficiency in one or more languages such as Rust or Python. Experience with machine learning frameworks like PyTorch is also required. The focus is on writing scalable, maintainable, and highly optimized code.
  • Inquisitive Problem-Solving & Tenacity: A demonstrated ability to tackle open-ended, ambiguous problems. You must be willing to experiment, fail, iterate, and relentlessly pursue solutions.
  • End-to-End Execution: The ability to own a project from the initial white-boarding of a research idea to the final deployment of a scalable production system.

Ways to Stand Out from the Crowd:

  • Safety & Security Background: Prior domain experience in Trust & Safety, cybersecurity, threat intelligence, adversarial machine learning, or content moderation.
  • Guardrails & Moderation: Hands-on experience developing, fine-tuning, or deploying models specifically built for harm detection, content safety (violence, hate, harassment, CBRNE, etc.) filtering, or run-time AI guardrails.

title: Senior Systems Software Engineer - Data Center Performance
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. It’s a unique legacy of innovation that’s fueled by great technology—and amazing people. Today, we’re tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in a diverse, supportive environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world.


We are hiring a proficient engineer to join our Applied Systems Engineering Performance team. This role integrates comprehensive experimentation and software engineering to explore how emerging platforms respond under demanding HPC and AI workloads. You will reveal performance restrictions, establish trustworthy measurements, and provide collaborating teams with the insights they need to improve new platforms. Your work will connect innovations in individual technologies with the challenge of harmonizing their performance at datacenter scale.


What you'll be doing:

  • Characterize node, rack, and cluster performance using microbenchmarks and representative applications. Measure throughput, latency, and scaling efficiency to identify compute, memory, communication, and storage bottlenecks.
  • Identify Linux performance problems related to CPU scheduling, NUMA locality, CPU and memory affinity, interrupt handling, and resource contention. Assess their impact on GPU usage and application efficiency.
  • Examine distributed workload scaling, considering collective communication, synchronization delays, slow nodes, and the interplay between computation and communication. Assess how GPU and NIC positioning, interconnect structure, and network traffic impact performance.
  • Combine application profiles, system traces, hardware counters, and cluster telemetry to isolate root causes. Develop focused reproductions and collaborate with hardware, firmware, driver, library, and application teams to implement and verify fixes.
  • Develop and maintain Python tools for automated benchmark execution, data collection, and performance analysis. Set up repeatable baselines, assess run-to-run variability, and spot regressions across hardware configurations and software releases.
  • Define and complete performance validation for new platforms and cluster deployments. Identify underperforming nodes, links, or storage paths, and verify that corrective actions restore encouraged workload performance.

What we need to see:

  • Extensive practical experience in Linux performance analysis, including knowledge of processes and threads, CPU and memory architecture, NUMA, I/O, and networking.
  • Experience investigating performance in multi-node HPC or GPU-accelerated systems, distinguishing local resource bottlenecks from communication overhead, load imbalance, and shared-resource contention.
  • Deep expertise in at least one relevant area: GPU application performance, Linux systems performance, high-speed networking and collective communication, parallel storage, or HPC performance tooling.
  • Proficiency in Python to build maintainable automation and analysis tools. Experience in developing and debugging performance-sensitive code in C, C++ and CUDA.
  • Ability to build controlled experiments, interpret profiling and counter data, and demonstrate reproducible improvements in application performance.
  • Independently driving technical efforts across hardware and software boundaries, communicating findings clearly, and working with component owners to resolve issues.
  • BS or MS in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Physics (or equivalent experience), with 8+ years of applicable experience.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Experience working with profiling and tracing tools like Nsight Systems, Nsight Compute, Linux perf, or eBPF-based tools.
  • Practical experience with RDMA and MPI or NCCL, and analyzing performance across PCIe, NVLink, InfiniBand, or Ethernet interconnects.
  • Experience with Slurm, container runtimes, and cgroups, including understanding how workload placement, resource isolation, and CPU/GPU/NIC affinity impact performance.
  • Experience improving distributed training, inference, or scientific applications by conducting strong- and weak-scaling studies, or building automated performance regression frameworks using tools such as ReFrame.

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and other objective job-related factors. The expected base salary ranges for this position are:
Poland: 292,500 PLN – 507,000 PLN for Level 4; and 375,000 PLN – 650,000 PLN for Level 5.
France: 87,750 EUR – 152,100 EUR for Level 4; and 114,000 EUR – 197,600 EUR for Level 5.
Germany: 112,200 EUR – 194,480 EUR for Level 4; and 141,900 EUR – 245,960 EUR for Level 5.

title: Senior SoC Architect, RAS
descriptionHtml:
We are now looking for a Senior Hardware Architect for our Tegra System-on-Chips (SoC) focused on Reliability, Availability, and Serviceability (RAS). Do you want to be part of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) revolution? Interested in defining resilient computing platforms for datacenters, autonomous vehicles, edge systems, and other high-reliability applications? We are looking for an exceptional SoC architect to help define, drive, and deliver RAS hardware architecture across advanced CPUs and SoCs, from early architectural concepts through design implementation, verification, validation, and production readiness.


This position offers the opportunity to have real impact in a dynamic, technology-focused company developing innovative processor and system architectures at the forefront of machine learning, autonomous vehicles, high-performance computing, and edge computing. Work with world-class systems architects, RAS experts, design teams, verification teams, validation teams, firmware teams, and software partners to define end-to-end hardware RAS features that improve system resiliency, observability, debuggability, error containment, recovery, and serviceability. Space and radiation-aware design are important areas of interest for this role, including understanding how radiation effects can influence SoC reliability, but the primary focus is broad SoC RAS architecture and driving features successfully through the product development flow.


What you’ll be doing:  

  • Define and drive SoC-level RAS hardware architecture across CPUs, interconnects, memory systems, IOs, safety islands, firmware interfaces, and platform-level components.
  • Own RAS features from concept through architecture specification, micro-architecture alignment, RTL implementation support, design verification, silicon validation, debug, and production readiness.
  • Develop architectural requirements for fault detection, correction, containment, isolation, telemetry, error reporting, recovery, graceful degradation, serviceability, and diagnostic observability.
  • Work closely with design, verification, validation, firmware, software, and platform teams to ensure RAS features are implementable, verifiable, debuggable, and aligned with system-level requirements.
  • Understand the broader SoC architecture and identify how RAS mechanisms interact with performance, power, reset flows, clocks, memory hierarchy, interconnect behavior, firmware-visible controls, and platform software.
  • Create hardware specifications, architectural requirements, error-handling flows, design guidance, test plans, and architectural models in SystemC, C/C++, Python, or other relevant modeling environments where applicable.
  • Plan and review verification and validation strategies for RAS mechanisms, including error injection, recovery validation, coverage analysis, resiliency modeling, and architecture reviews.
  • Assist in failure analysis and silicon debug for lab, post-silicon, production, and field findings; develop diagnostic screens and localization methods for latent, intermittent, and environment-sensitive failures.
  • Apply RAS architecture principles to high-reliability deployment environments. This includes space-aware and radiation-aware use cases where single-event effects, memory corruption, logic corruption, or cumulative radiation exposure may impact system reliability.
  • Follow industry standards and research related to RAS, functional safety, semiconductor reliability, debuggability, verification, validation, and silicon testing.
  • Patent novel hardware architecture techniques that improve system resiliency, observability, serviceability, and recovery.

What we need to see:  

  • MS or PhD degree in computer engineering, electrical engineering, or equivalent experience.
  • At least 8+ years of SoC architecture, design, verification, reliability, silicon validation, or related hardware development experience.
  • Strong understanding of Reliability, Availability, and Serviceability (RAS) in the SoC context, including fault detection, correction, containment, telemetry, recovery, degradation modes, debug visibility, and serviceability mechanisms.
  • Experience defining and driving hardware architecture features through the full development lifecycle, including architecture definition, design implementation, verification planning, validation, debug, and production readiness.
  • Strong understanding of overall SoC architecture and the ability to reason across micro-architecture, full-chip integration, firmware interfaces, software-visible behavior, platform flows, and customer use cases.
  • Meaningful industry expertise in one or more SoC architecture areas such as RAS, safety, debug, clocks, resets, interconnects, memory controllers, IO technologies, platform integration, firmware-visible error handling, or diagnostic infrastructure.
  • Hands-on experience with design verification, silicon validation, fault injection, coverage analysis, resiliency modeling, diagnostic development, or reliability validation methodology.
  • Familiarity with radiation effects, space operation, or other high-reliability deployment environments is strongly valued, including understanding how hardware architecture can mitigate single-event effects and related reliability risks.
  • Excellent analytical, written, and verbal interpersonal skills with the ability to work effectively across architecture, design, verification, firmware, software, validation, and customer-facing teams.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:  

  • Demonstrated history of architecting and delivering complex SoC RAS features across design, verification, validation, and production phases.
  • Deep familiarity with architectural resiliency techniques such as ECC, parity, redundancy, replay, checkpoint/restart, scrubbing, isolation, containment, telemetry, error logging, recovery flows, and graceful degradation.
  • Experience with debug of hardware failures in simulation, emulation, post-silicon validation, production, customer deployments, or other high-reliability systems.
  • Familiarity with Design for Debug, Design for Test, Design for Reliability, silicon observability, fault-injection methodology, and coverage driven validation flows.

NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers. We have some of the most forward-thinking and hardworking people in the world working for us. If you are creative, autonomous, and motivated to define and deliver resilient SoC architectures that improve reliability, debuggability, and serviceability across demanding applications, we want to hear from you!

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and other objective job-related factors. The expected base salary ranges for this position are:
184,000 USD – 287,500 USD for Level 4; and 224,000 USD – 356,500 USD for Level 5.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

title: Senior Firmware Application Engineer - System Software

  • Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively in dynamic environments and translate technical requirements and challenges into actionable solutions.

  • Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and adapt to changing business needs.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Strong understanding of server architecture, platform management, and data center technologies.

title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, AI Safety Evaluations
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA has helped redefine what computers can do. Now, generative AI is opening new possibilities for how people learn, create, and tackle problems. Realizing that potential means answering some of the hardest questions in AI: Where do models fall short? Which risks are we missing? How do we know our safeguards are working? As an expert in machine learning for Evaluations, you’ll help establish the evidence that guides the next generation of safer AI. Your curiosity and scientific judgment can shape what we test, what we learn, and what we build next.


We are looking for a Machine Learning Engineer / AI Researcher / Data Scientist to join our AI Safety and Responsibility efforts within Enterprise Risk Management. Engaging directly in engineering tasks, you will apply your data science and statistics skills. You will turn open research questions into rigorous benchmarks, inventive experiments, and tools that reveal how multimodal large language models behave under pressure. Working with researchers and platform engineers, you’ll connect those discoveries to better training methods and safeguards, with reproducible results that inform technical reviews and executive decisions. If you love asking the question no one has thought to test, and building a convincing way to answer it, come help us define what progress in AI safety looks like.


What You Will Be Doing:

  • Safety Benchmarking: Design and maintain safety benchmarks for large language and multimodal models, translating risk scenarios into test cases, datasets, and scoring rubrics.
  • Evaluation Methodology: Define metrics and protocols that assess safety alongside model usefulness, using baselines, uncertainty estimates, and failure analysis to distinguish meaningful improvements from noise.
  • Reproducible Evaluation: Build reusable Python pipelines with versioned datasets, model configurations, and experiment tracking to reproduce results and compare performance across model releases.
  • Automated Red-Teaming: Develop tools to discover failure modes and expand evaluation coverage, incorporating human review to validate automated scoring and provide additional judgment.
  • Failure Analysis: Investigate model failures with researchers, document actionable findings, and develop regression tests to assess whether model changes resolve identified issues.
  • Results and Communication: Partner with platform engineers to store and aggregate evaluation results, and clearly communicate findings, limitations, and emerging risks to researchers and decision-makers.

What We Need To See:

  • Education and Experience: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience, with 6+ years in the field of machine learning engineering or evaluation.
  • Evaluation Design: Experience developing benchmarks, metrics, and statistically sound comparisons for ML systems, including selecting baselines and interpreting uncertainty.  Ability to translate ambiguous evaluation questions into testable experiments.
  • Engineering: Strong Python skills and experience building maintainable shared tools, data pipelines, and experiment-tracking workflows.
  • Analytical Rigor: Ability to assess dataset quality, identify limitations in metrics and scoring methods, and support conclusions with reproducible evidence.
  • Communication: Clearly explain findings and tradeoffs to researchers, engineering partners, and executives.

Ways to Stand Out from the Crowd:

  • Evaluation: Experience evaluating LLMs, multimodal models, or agentic systems through adversarial testing or automated red-teaming.
  • Community Contributions: Contributions to public benchmarks or evaluation frameworks.
  • Research Publications: A publication track record and interest in continuing to publish at top tier venues.
  • Human-Aligned Evaluation: Experience validating model-based evaluators against human judgments or designing human-in-the-loop evaluation workflows.
  • Statistical Rigor: Strong model evaluation skills and a commitment to sound statistical practices, including confidence intervals.
Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and other objective job-related factors. The expected base salary ranges for this position are:
184,000 USD – 287,500 USD for Level 4; and 224,000 USD – 356,500 USD for Level 5.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

title: Senior Software Developer, AI Networking
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA is changing the world of AI Networking with groundbreaking technology. We are excited to be adding an AI Networking Software Developer to our AI Networking SW development and codesign team. We are working with the latest NVIDIA hardware and technologies. We do full stack benchmarking for Data Center scale systems for AI training/inference and lower level benchmarks. We strive for automation and develop many tools in-house yet adopt community accepted practices and frameworks. Moreover we give back to community developing our own tools in public GitHub repositories. Our goal is to ensure that large-scale systems deliver expected performance in practice, not just on paper, by uncovering bottlenecks and driving continuous improvements.


What you'll be doing:

  • Developing AI networking communication frameworks and applications running in production on the world’s largest supercomputers and data centers.
  • Develop production tools and benchmarks used by multiple teams inside and outside NVIDIA.
  • Enable new AI models within our benchmarking infrastructure and deliver insights through end-to-end analysis of large-scale workloads across hardware and software stacks.
  • Design and implement automation systems, including large-scale parameter search to identify optimal configurations across complex systems.
  • Collaborate closely with networking and hardware teams to co-design new features and software interfaces in a fast-paced, evolving environment.

What we need to see:

  • B.Sc., M.Sc degree in Computer Science / Software engineering or equivalent experience.
  • 5+ years of experience.
  • Professional Python development experience. We seek individuals who build maintainable, long-lived tools that do not impose a heavy burden on the team in terms of maintenance.
  • Solid Linux expertise and passion for working extensively in command-line environments.
  • Ability to work across a broad and evolving stack, with a strong drive to learn—from hardware and networking up to large-scale AI systems running across entire clusters

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Familiarity with cluster orchestration systems such as Slurm or Kubernetes.
  • Knowledge in MPI and HPC, InfiniBand, Ethernet and Networking.
  • Experience in performance optimizations

For two decades, we have pioneered visual computing, and the art and science of computer graphics.
